title: Modulating Shape of Polyester Based Polymersomes using Osmotic Pressure
protocol: Dissolve polyesters PEG-PLA or PEG-b-poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) in DMSO at a concentration of 1.5% weight.
Vortex for up to 15 minutes if full dissolution is required.
Set up the solvent injection apparatus with a stir plate below the vertical syringe pump.
Place a 5 mL glass vial containing 1 mL of Type II deionized water and a miniature stir bar on the stir plate.
Adjust the syringe pump's height to allow the needle tip to be fully immersed in the water.
Set the infusion rate of the syringe pump to 5 µL/min.
Draw the organic solvent and polyester solution into a 27 G needle with a ½" needle length.
Place the needle into the syringe pump securely.
Start the stir plate at 100 rpm and begin the syringe pump.
Remove the glass vial from the stir bar once infusion is complete, then cap it.
Prepare for dynamic light scattering (DLS) analysis.
Take 1 mL of water containing organic solvent and polymer into a cuvette.
Insert the cuvette into the DLS system as per Table 1 settings.
Perform DLS to measure polymersome intensity-weighted diameter and polydispersity index (PDI).
Confirm spherical polymersome formation using Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM) and Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM).
Optimize TEM protocols for use at 120 kV if necessary.
Optimize SEM protocols for use at 5.0 kV if necessary.
Apply uranyl acetate as a background stain if polymersomes are not visible using EM.
Wash a 300 kDa dialysis membrane according to manufacturer's instructions.
Add 1 mL of polymersome solution into the reservoir of the dialysis device.
Place the dialysis device in a 250 mL beaker with 150 mL of Type II deionized water on a stir plate.
Set the stir plate to a speed that allows for gentle movement of the dialysis device and leave to stir overnight.
Decrease the speed if a vortex is formed during dialysis.
Extract the 1 mL polymersome solution from the dialysis device after completion.
Characterize the polymersome solution following step 1.5.
Create 150 mL of desired salt buffer with either 50 mM, 100 mM, or 200 mM concentration of sodium chloride based on final properties.
Place the polymersome solution into a dialysis device and load it into 150 mL of the desired salt solution.
Allow to gently stir for 18 hours.
Shape-modulated polymersomes can be stored in isotonic solutions for up to 7 days.
Perform polymersome characterization via DLS.
Perform polymersome characterization via TEM.
Perform polymersome characterization via SEM.
Apply uranyl acetate as a background stain if polymersomes are not visible using EM.
Pay particular attention to PDI measurements compared to spherical polymersomes when performing DLS measurements.
Use appropriate controls for imaging, especially non-shape modulated polymersomes.
